claim: Lower or looser prefrontal control helps open-ended idea generation and strong control helps closed tasks (matched filter), but the human evidence is mixed: it rests on reviews, small tDCS studies and one fMRI study.
agent_test: Run each task with a tight-constraint prompt and a relaxed-constraint prompt on closed (convergent) and open (divergent) items at equal tokens; check the crossover.

claim: Working-memory capacity correlates only weakly with creativity (r = .083, k = 28, n = 3104; Gong 2023). In the larger memory meta-analysis (79 studies, 525 effects, N = 12,846; Gerver 2023) working memory r = .17 and overall memory r = .19, with no small-study bias (Egger p = .76). Semantic memory (r = .25) matters more than control capacity.
agent_test: Vary reasoning budget or context load; test whether originality moves with it. Expect a small effect.

claim: Default-network and executive-network coupling during creative generation is supported by fMRI (N = 25, global efficiency r = .44) and a large ALE meta-analysis (787 experiments); this is a co-operation view, not a pure trade-off.
agent_test: Run a generate pass (loose) followed by a separate evaluate pass (strict) versus a single pass, at equal tokens.

claim: Inhibition and cognitive flexibility predict creative output in some studies (Benedek 2012 SEM, flanker study 2026) but fluency often shows no effect, and findings depend on task and intelligence control.
agent_test: Test whether an explicit 'suppress the obvious answer' step raises originality score without lowering validity.

claim: tDCS effects on creativity are inconsistent: site, polarity, expertise and task all change the sign (Rosen 2016 expertise interaction, Khalil 2020 originality, Pena 2022 mixed), and recent null or adverse effects exist. Meta-analytic view: only anodal left lateral frontal stimulation helps reliably (divergent d = .54, CI touching zero; convergent d = .40; 20 creativity studies); the 32-study 2024 meta-analysis found gains for convergent but not divergent thinking overall.
agent_test: Do not hard-code a single 'relax control' rule; make constraint level depend on the agent's task familiarity (novice vs expert).

claim: Rosen et al. (2016): anodal right DLPFC helped less experienced jazz pianists and hurt the most experienced (interaction p = .002 to .043 across two reports; N = 17). Two searches found no direct replication; Khalil 2023 (N = 40) shows trait moderation of IFG stimulation, a partial parallel only.
agent_test: Compare constraint relaxation on familiar versus unfamiliar problem classes.

claim: Raising LLM sampling temperature gives only weak gains in novelty (slope .308) and some loss of coherence (.240); temperature is not a creativity dial.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare temperature rise versus structured constraint relaxation (prompt level) on novelty and coherence.

claim: GPT-4 can exceed the average human on the Divergent Association Task (85.6 at temperature 1.5, above 72% of humans) but top-decile humans stay above all models.
agent_test: Score agent output with DAT/AUT against human norms, with and without a generate-then-evaluate split.

claim: LLMs are homogeneous in open-ended output (mode collapse; top-10 words are 25.5% of tokens); CreativityNeuro weight steering lowers this by 10.2 points and raises DAT by up to 14 human percentiles, with an MMLU cost of about 3 points. No replication on larger or closed models was found; protecting MMLU in the mask did not protect MMLU (-0.71 pp more).
agent_test: Add a diversity operator (forced distinct branches, banned-answer list) and measure unique-answer rate at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show poor human-like executive control in classic tasks (WCST 0.29 to 0.53 vs 0.77 human, Flanker incongruent 40 to 60% vs 93 to 96%), with accuracy dropping with list length and dialogue length.
agent_test: Insert an explicit conflict check or rule-restatement step each few turns and see if perseveration drops.

claim: Prompt structure restores executive control in LLMs: chain-of-thought plus text input lifted WCST categories from about 0.02-0.08 to 0.92-1.00, and reasoning models raised Flanker incongruent accuracy, though not WCST in one study; findings conflict on WCST. Reasoning-trained models are less diverse in creative writing (28 LLMs), but prompted CoT reduced fixation in ideation (slope 1.023 to 1.354).
agent_test: Test the CoT-with-rule-exclusivity prompt on a rule-switching task versus plain prompt.

claim: A modular planner with an explicit Monitor (conflict monitoring) improves planning: removing Monitor raised invalid moves from 0% to 31%; Tower of Hanoi 3-disk about 7x zero-shot.
agent_test: Ablate a monitor step at equal tokens on planning tasks.

claim: LLM internal representations align with human DMN activity during creative tasks more for larger models (r = .55 on creative task vs r = .09 on control task), and alignment with DMN, not with the control network, tracks AUT score.
agent_test: Not directly testable; treat as background.

claim: Evidence that the prefrontal-versus-default relation changes with age or culture is thin: culture moderates the WM-creativity link (Q = 4.26, p = .039), and children do not show less cognitive-control engagement in one small fMRI study (N = 15 vs 16).

Separating a loose, goal-free generate pass from a constrained select pass raised originality in an agent benchmark (AUT originality 2.91 to 3.77; path success 48.2% to 67.9% with Reflect plus ReDNA on GPT-5.4). Not tested at equal tokens.
agent_test: Rerun a two-call diverge-then-select against a single-call prompt at the same total token budget on AUT and a correctness task.

claim: The in-loop selector sets the outcome of generate-then-select creativity: more iterations gave no gain (3.921/3.835/3.927 at 5/15/30), and a smaller selector beat a larger one.
agent_test: Vary selector strictness and size in the select step; score novelty and correctness separately.

claim: Reasoning-mode post-training narrows creative output: collapse is set in the weights by training data (Think-SFT loses 62% of base diversity) and turning off CoT at inference does not restore diversity.
agent_test: Compare a reasoning model with its instruct sibling on AUT at equal tokens; do not expect a no-think switch to restore diversity.

claim: Injected irrelevant or random context raises LLM-judged novelty or category spread on AUT, but each context type moves a different metric and quality is unchecked; no test of attention leakiness or of cost on correctness exists.
agent_test: Add one off-topic seed to the generate pass only; measure novelty and relevance with a blind judge.

claim: No study links LLM executive-function scores (WCST, Flanker, Stroop) to originality across models, and no preregistered replication of Chrysikou 2011/2013 was found; both remain open.
agent_test: Score a model set on Flanker and AUT; check rank correlation.
